   C. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR VINCENT LUGO PARK NEW
  PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-03

  This item is to award a construction contract for $124,155 to the lowest
  responsive bidder, Ortco, Incorporated (Contractor) for the Vincent Lugo Park
  New Playground Equipment Project. The project will install new play
  equipment (for ages 2-12) in the two new playground areas at Vincent Lugo
  Park. The installation also includes an ADA accessible concrete walkway,
  perimeter curbs, curb ramps, wood fiber playground surfacing, sump trench
  drains, and playground signage, which will complete Phase 2 of the Vincent
  Lugo Park Renovation Project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Vincent Lugo Park New
  Playground Equipment Project, Contract No. 20-03;
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute contract documents with Ortco,
  Incorporated for total bid amount in the amount of $124,155;
  3. Approve a Purchase Order in the amount of $136,571 which includes a
  10% construction contingency; and
  4. Approve a separate Purchase Order for San Gabriel Valley Conservation
  Corps in the amount of $3,360 for turf removal.

5.  PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6.  NEW BUSINESS

  A. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR TASK FORCE FOR REGIONAL
  AUTO THEFT PREVENTION

  Police Department staff has researched the feasibility and benefits of entering
  into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the “Taskforce for
  Regional Auto Theft Prevention” (T.R.A.P.) to combat vehicle theft, vehicle
  embezzlement, and the ancillary criminal activities associated with the
  aforementioned crimes. The MOU serves as an operative document
  governing T.R.A.P. operations and was studied to determine the benefits,
  costs, risks and opportunities associated with participation.

  Recommended Action:

 City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – May 5, 2020  3
   Staff recommends assigning one Detective to the Taskforce for Regional Auto
  Theft Prevention Program and authorizing the City Manager to enter into the
  Memorandum of Understanding.

  B. CONSIDERATION TO REPEAL URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 668
  TEMPORARILY RESRICTING RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL EVICTIONS
  FOR NONPAYMENT OF RENT DUE TO COVID-19

  After the adoption of Urgency Ordinance No. 668, state and county
  authorities issued new rules and orders that afford even greater protections
  to residential and commercial tenants impacted by COVID-19. The new
  County Order is effectively retroactively to March 5 and covers all residential
  and commercial tenants in Los Angeles County, and applies to
  unincorporated areas and incorporated cities, except cities that have a local
  eviction moratoria in place.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider repealing Urgency
  Ordinance No. 668 in its entirety, in light of recent actions taken at the state
  and county level affording greater protections to residential and commercial
  tenants during the COVID-19 emergency and to avoid conflicts and
  ambiguities between the City’s eviction moratorium and subsequent orders
  and rules issued by county and state officials.

  C. PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT UPDATE

  The Public Works Department will be presenting an update to Council
  regarding accomplishments, staffing and organizational changes, operational
  improvements, completed and proposed budget-saving efforts, and future
  plans. The presentation will highlight the department’s efforts to operate
  more efficiently and describe how the department has decreased
  expenditures over the past year.

MINUTES OF MAY 5, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:35 p.m. on Tuesday, May 5, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Pu.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux,  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

Mayor Menchaca provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objections to the Agenda Order, Mayor Menchaca stated the Agenda
  Order was approved.
2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. PROCLAMATION OF THE MONTH OF MAY AS NATIONAL PRESERVATION
  MONTH

  Presentation was made by Assistant City Manager/Community Development Director
  Arminé Chaparyan.

  B. COVID-19 UPDATE ON CITY OPERATIONS

  Mayor Menchaca announced that this will be an ongoing presentation on the
  Agenda until the COVID-19 epidemic ends to keep the public informed directly
  from the City’s first responders and staff.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  May 5, 2020
   Presentations were made by Fire Chief Wallace, Police Chief Harris, Community
  Services/ Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez, and City Manager Lazzaretto.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Council Member Pu pulled Item 4A(2) and 4C for separate discussion.

  Regarding Item 4A(2), he requested greater clarification on the Minutes of the Regular
  Meeting of April 21, 2020, on Item 6A as to the first half of the recommendation that
  was approved and the second half of the recommendation that was deferred.

  Regarding Item 4C, he received additional information from Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez relative to the layout of the
  playground equipment.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A(1) and 4B – 4C as presented, and Item 4A(2) as amended.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A(1) and 4B – 4C as presented, and Item
  4A(2) as amended by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following item as presented:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of April 7, 2020.

  The City Council approved the following item as amended:
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of April 21, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the April 10, 2020, and April 17, 2020 Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR VINCENT LUGO PARK NEW
  PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT PROJECT, CONTRACT NO. 20-03

  The City Council:
  1. Approved plans and specifications for the Vincent Lugo Park New Playground
  Equipment Project, Contract No. 20-03;
  2. Authorized the City Manager to execute contract documents with Ortco,
  Incorporated for total bid amount in the amount of $124,155;
  3. Approved a Purchase Order in the amount of $136,571 which includes a 10%
  construction contingency; and
  4. Approved a separate Purchase Order for San Gabriel Valley Conservation Corps
  in the amount of $3,360 for turf removal.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  May 5, 2020
 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR TASK FORCE FOR REGIONAL
  AUTO THEFT PREVENTION (T.R.A.P.)

  The staff presentation was made by Police Chief Eugene Harris.

  Debbie Kilgore, resident, questioned if the officer assigned to T.R.A.P. would be
  pulled from regular hours with the San Gabriel Police Department.

  Discussion included a net savings for the City for the assigned officer’s salary,
  benefits and vehicle cost; the City’s ability to call the officer back from the task
  force for City duties as needed; rotation of where task force officers are based;
  assignment of a detective with experience in this field of law enforcement; no loss
  of capacity to investigate crimes in San Gabriel; greater access to regional
  resources; criteria for participation; regional representation; and outside funding
  for the task force.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Harrington,
  to approve the assignment of one Detective to the Taskforce for Regional Auto
  Theft Prevention Program and authorize the City Manager to enter into the
  Memorandum of Understanding.

  Motion approved New Business Item 6A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. CONSIDERATION TO REPEAL URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 668 TEMPORARILY
  RESTRICTING RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL EVICTIONS FOR
  NONPAYMENT OF RENT DUE TO COVID-19

  City Attorney Lemieux explained that there is no conflict of interest for Council
  Member Pu, as an owner of residential rental property, and Council Member Ding,
  as an owner of commercial property, to participate in this item as the action applies
  equally to all leases in the City and is undertaken under an emergency declaration.

  The staff presentation was made by Deputy City Attorney Norma Tabares.

  The following provided public comment in opposition to repealing the ordinance
  and requested it instead be tailored for San Gabriel: Danielle Leidner-Peretz,
  representing the Apartment Association of Greater Los Angeles; Isaac Hung, rental
  property owner; and Matthew Buck, representing the California Apartment
  Association.

  The following provided public comment in favor of repealing the ordinance: Teresa
  Eilers, West San Gabriel Valley Organizer for United Way’s Everyone In Campaign;
  Eric Sunada, San Gabriel Valley Oversight Group; Sean McMorris, resident; Rev. Rae
  Chen Huang; and Paul Cole Padilla, resident.

  The following also provided public comment: Judy Liu.

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  May 5, 2020
   Discussion included timeframes and differences between San Gabriel’s (City’s)
  urgency ordinance and the County’s similar ordinance; preference to incorporate
  County provisions as desired into a revised City ordinance rather than repealing
  the City’s ordinance; preference to maintain local authority; consideration for both
  tenants and landlords; timeframes given in Executive Order No. 37-20 relative to
  the City’s ordinance; pros and cons of revising San Gabriel’s ordinance versus
  repealing it in favor of the County’s ordinance; preference to repeal San Gabriel’s
  ordinance; staff time and cost involved in serving residents relative to the City’s
  versus the County’s ordinance; the County having dedicated resources and
  assistance hotlines relative to this matter; whether repealing this City ordinance
  precludes the ability to adopt another in the future; the City having no authority
  with banks relative to loans; litigation concerns; federal loan protections; use of
  CDBG funds to subsidize rent for qualified recipients; working with non-profits and
  community groups to assist those in need of rent assistance; and the ability to
  bring back a revised City ordinance for consideration at a future time.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to
  repeal Urgency Ordinance No. 668 in its entirety.

  Motion failed by a vote of 2-3 as follows:
  AYES:  PU, MENCHACA
  NOES:  DING, HARRINGTON, LIAO
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Following additional discussion, there was a consensus of the City Council to have
  the City Attorney and City Manager prepare a revised City ordinance with input
  from Council Members for consideration at the May 21, 2020 regular City Council
  meeting.

  C. PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT UPDATE

  Presentation was made by Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck.

  Council Members commended Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck for a
  job well-done and for realizing savings for the City while improving the quality of
  services.

  There were no public comments.

7. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto gave a reminder about the Special Budget Meeting to be held
  on May 12, 2020, at 5:30 p.m.
9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Liao reported on donations of personal protective equipment (PPE) that
  have been received and distributed.

  Council Member Ding thanked the Fire and Police Departments for keeping the City
  safe, commented on donations of PPE, and reminded residents to stay home, stay
  healthy, and stay safe.
